# Mapping catalog reference

<!-- Generated by `python -m tools.mapping_reference`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every packaged framework catalog and rule, as `python -m shadowscan.mappings.validate`
checks them. References are evidence references, not compliance determinations,
and the rules are author mappings, not independently reviewed. See
[Threat and control mappings](mappings.md) for how findings use them.

## Catalogs

`Checked` is the date a catalog was compiled and its entries last checked.
A `primary` catalog was checked against the source it links. A `secondary`
catalog links the framework's own publication, which could not be consulted;
its entries follow secondary sources.

### `eu-ai-act-2024`

EU AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, edition 2024.

Publication: <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj> (not consulted directly; entries follow secondary sources)

Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (reported by secondary sources; the Official Journal could not be retrieved). Which obligations apply depends on the system's risk class and the operator's role, which ShadowScan cannot determine; a reference is evidence relevant to an article, not a finding that the article applies or is met.

| `eu-ai-act-2024:Art.26` | Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems |

### `maestro-2025`

CSA MAESTRO agentic threat modelling layers, edition 2025.

Publication: <https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/blog/2025/02/06/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-framework-maestro> (not consulted directly; entries follow secondary sources)

Seven-layer reference architecture published by the Cloud Security Alliance in February 2025. The publication itself could not be retrieved; layer labels follow secondary sources, which differ slightly on layers 4 to 6. Layer 6 is cross-cutting. A layer says where in the stack a finding sits; it is not a threat identifier.

| Reference | Title |
| --- | --- |
| `maestro-2025:L1` | Foundation Models |
| `maestro-2025:L2` | Data Operations |
| `maestro-2025:L3` | Agent Frameworks |
| `maestro-2025:L4` | Deployment and Infrastructure |
| `maestro-2025:L5` | Evaluation and Observability |
| `maestro-2025:L6` | Security and Compliance |
| `maestro-2025:L7` | Agent Ecosystem |

## Rules

A rule applies when every clause of its condition holds. Threat and layer rules
feed `metadata.threats`; control rules feed `metadata.controls`.

### Threat rules

From `shadowscan/mappings/data/rules/threats.yaml`.

| Rule | When | References | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool-poisoning` | tag `tool-poisoning` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM01`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI01`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0110.000`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0051.001` | A tool description carrying injected instructions is read by the model as trusted context and can redirect the agent's goal. |
| `unsafe-serialization` | tag `unsafe-serialization` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM04`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI04`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0011.000`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0010.003` | A model artifact in a format that can execute code on load is a supply chain risk for anyone who loads it. |
| `credential-exposure` | tag `hardcoded-credential` or `inline-secrets` or `plaintext-credential` or `secret-in-env` or `unmasked-ci-variable` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM02`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI03`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0055` | A credential stored in source, configuration or an unmasked variable can be read and reused by anyone who can read that location. |
| `credential-finding` | kind `secret` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI03` | An AI provider credential, wherever it is stored, is an identity that an agent or anyone who obtains it can act as. |
| `agent-config-credentials` | tag `hardcoded-credential` or `inline-secrets` or `plaintext-credential` or `secret-in-env` or `unmasked-ci-variable`; and kind `agent-config` or `mcp-server` | `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0083` | Credentials kept in an agent or MCP configuration file are the target of credential collection from agent configuration. |
| `privileged-workload` | tag `cluster-admin` or `policy.privileged-scopes` or `privileged-pod` or `wildcard-permissions` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI03` | Administrative or wildcard privileges give an agent, or whoever controls it, more authority than its task needs. |
| `privileged-pod-escape` | tag `privileged-pod` | `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0105` | A privileged pod can reach the node it runs on, a precondition for escaping the AI workload to the host. |
| `code-execution-capability` | capability `code-exec` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI05`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0050` | An agent that can run code or shell commands turns a hijacked goal into command execution. |
| `code-execution-configuration` | tag `mcp-shell-command` or `posture-unrestricted-shell` or `remote-code-fetch` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI05`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0050` | Configuration that starts tools through a shell, permits any command or downloads and runs code gives the agent a command interpreter. |
| `saas-actions` | capability `saas-actions` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI02`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0053` | An agent that can act in SaaS applications can be steered into misusing those tools. |
| `approval-bypass` | tag `mcp-auto-approve` or `posture-permissions-bypassed` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI02`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI09` | Tool calls that run without per-call approval remove the human check that would catch a misused tool. |
| `unsandboxed-agent` | tag `posture-unsandboxed` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI05`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0105` | An agent running outside its sandbox executes code directly on the host. |
| `exposed-ai-service` | tag `exposed-llm-server` or `no-authentication` or `posture-exposed-gateway` or `posture-unauthenticated-gateway` or `public-ingress` or `public-principal` or `unauthenticated-mcp` | `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0132` | A service reachable beyond its intended boundary, or without authentication, is a misconfigured or publicly exposed AI service. |
| `exposed-inference-server` | tag `exposed-llm-server` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM06`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0040` | An inference server reachable by others gives them model access and lets them consume its capacity. |
| `unauthenticated-endpoint` | tag `no-authentication` or `posture-unauthenticated-gateway` or `unauthenticated-mcp` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI03` | An agent endpoint without authentication cannot tell which identity is acting through it. |
| `mcp-unpinned-package` | tag `mcp-unpinned-package` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM04`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI04`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0010.005`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0109` | An MCP server resolved to whatever version is current can change under the agent after it was reviewed. |
| `mcp-broad-filesystem` | tag `mcp-broad-filesystem` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI02`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0086` | A filesystem tool scoped to the whole disk or a home directory lets a steered agent read and send files outside its task. |
| `mcp-unvetted-source` | tag `mcp-registry-deleted` or `mcp-unpublished` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM04`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI04`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0010.005` | An MCP server that no configured MCP registry lists, or that its registry marks deleted, has no registry provenance to review. |
| `hidden-instructions` | tag `hidden-instructions` or `invisible-text` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM01`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI01`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0051.001`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0068` | Instruction content hidden from the rendered view reaches the model but not the reviewer. |
| `memory-capability` | capability `memory` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI06`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0080.000` | Persistent agent memory can carry poisoned content into later sessions. |
| `rag-capability` | capability `rag` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM09`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI06`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0070` | Retrieval-augmented generation feeds indexed content into the context, where poisoned documents act as instructions. |
| `browsing-capability` | capability `browsing` | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM01`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0051.001` | An agent that reads web pages takes untrusted content into its context, the channel for indirect prompt injection. |
| `multi-agent-capability` | capability `multi-agent` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI07`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI08`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0118` | Agents that exchange messages can pass a compromise or a fault from one agent to the next. |
| `delegated-identity-capability` | capability `delegated-identity` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI03` | An agent acting with a user's delegated identity can be used to exercise that user's privileges. |
| `agent-card-without-security-scheme` | tag `no-auth-declared` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI07`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI03` | An A2A Agent Card that declares no security scheme invites peers to call the agent without authenticating. |
| `a2a-plaintext-interface` | tag `a2a-plaintext-interface` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI07`, `mitre-atlas-2026.09:AML.T0118.001` | An A2A interface over plaintext HTTP lets anyone on the network path read or alter the messages agents exchange directly. |
| `a2a-card-signature-invalid` | tag `a2a-card-signature-invalid` | `owasp-asi-2026:ASI07`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI04` | An Agent Card whose signature is malformed or does not verify may have been altered after signing, so peers cannot rely on the identity, endpoints and skills it advertises. |
| `high-autonomy` | `metadata.autonomy.floor` at least 4 | `owasp-llm-2026:LLM03`, `owasp-asi-2026:ASI08` | Evidence places the agent at high or full autonomy, where actions run without per-step human review and errors can compound. |

### Layer rules

From `shadowscan/mappings/data/rules/layers.yaml`.

| Rule | When | References | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maestro-l1-local-model` | kind `local-model` | `maestro-2025:L1` | Model weights stored for a local runtime are part of the foundation model layer. |
| `maestro-l1-model-artifact` | tag `unsafe-serialization` | `maestro-2025:L1` | An unsafe model serialization format is a property of the model artifact itself. |
| `maestro-l2-data` | capability `data-access` or `rag` | `maestro-2025:L2` | Retrieval and broad data access place the finding in the data operations layer. |
| `maestro-l3-agent-framework` | kind `agent` or `agent-config` or `framework-usage` or `mcp-server` or `workflow` | `maestro-2025:L3` | Agents, agent frameworks, agent and MCP configuration and AI workflows form the agent framework layer. |
| `maestro-l4-infrastructure` | kind `infra` or `runtime-process` | `maestro-2025:L4` | Infrastructure definitions and running processes sit in the deployment and infrastructure layer. |
| `maestro-l4-infrastructure-posture` | tag `cluster-admin` or `exposed-llm-server` or `no-egress-policy` or `privileged-pod` | `maestro-2025:L4` | Workload privilege, egress and exposure settings are deployment and infrastructure posture. |
| `maestro-l5-gateway-caller` | kind `gateway-caller` | `maestro-2025:L5` | A caller seen in gateway logs is an observation from the observability layer. |
| `maestro-l5-logging` | tag `no-diagnostic-logging` or `no-invocation-logging` or `tracing-disabled` | `maestro-2025:L5` | Disabled invocation logging or tracing is a gap in the evaluation and observability layer. |
| `maestro-l6-identity-and-credentials` | kind `iam-grant` or `oauth-grant` or `secret` or `service-identity` or `token` | `maestro-2025:L6` | Credentials, tokens, grants and service identities belong to the cross-cutting security layer. |
| `maestro-l7-multi-agent` | capability `multi-agent` | `maestro-2025:L7` | Agents that communicate with other agents take part in the agent ecosystem layer. |
| `maestro-l7-bot-app` | kind `bot-app` | `maestro-2025:L7` | A bot or app installed into a SaaS workspace operates in the agent ecosystem layer. |
| `maestro-l7-agent-card` | tag `no-auth-declared` | `maestro-2025:L7` | An A2A Agent Card advertises the agent to the agent ecosystem. |

### Control rules

From `shadowscan/mappings/data/rules/controls.yaml`.

| Rule | When | References | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shadow-ai-system` | shadow (not in the inventory) | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-1.6`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.4.2`, `aiuc-1-2026q2:E` | An AI system missing from the supplied inventory is evidence about the completeness of AI system inventory and resource documentation. |
| `registry-gap` | `metadata.registry_reconciliation.status` `observed-not-registered` | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-1.6`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.4.2` | An agent observed in the environment but absent from its registry is a gap in the AI system inventory. |
| `stale-registration` | `metadata.registry_reconciliation.status` `registered-not-observed` | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-1.7` | A registered agent that was not observed may be retired without being removed, which is relevant to decommissioning processes. |
| `missing-owner` | kind `agent` or `agent-config` or `ai-app` or `bot-app` or `cloud-resource` or `framework-usage` or `mcp-server` or `workflow`; and no owner recorded | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-2.1`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.3.2`, `aiuc-1-2026q2:E` | An AI system without a recorded owner has no documented accountability. |
| `oversight-bypassed` | `metadata.autonomy.oversight` `bypassed` | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-3.2`, `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:MAP-3.5`, `eu-ai-act-2024:Art.14`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.9.2`, `aiuc-1-2026q2:D003` | Evidence that the agent's human approval step is bypassed is relevant to human oversight and to restricting unsafe tool calls. |
| `high-autonomy-oversight` | `metadata.autonomy.floor` at least 4 | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-3.2`, `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:MAP-3.5`, `eu-ai-act-2024:Art.14`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.9.2`, `aiuc-1-2026q2:D003` | An agent operating at high or full autonomy depends on defined oversight measures rather than per-step review. |
| `logging-gap` | tag `no-diagnostic-logging` or `no-invocation-logging` or `tracing-disabled` | `eu-ai-act-2024:Art.12`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.6.2.8`, `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:MEASURE-3.1` | Disabled invocation logging or tracing removes the records that event logging and risk tracking rely on. |
| `security-exposure` | tag `exposed-llm-server` or `hardcoded-credential` or `inline-secrets` or `no-authentication` or `plaintext-credential` or `policy.privileged-scopes` or `posture-exposed-gateway` or `posture-unauthenticated-gateway` or `public-ingress` or `public-principal` or `secret-in-env` or `unauthenticated-mcp` or `unmasked-ci-variable` or `wildcard-permissions` | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:MEASURE-2.7`, `eu-ai-act-2024:Art.15`, `aiuc-1-2026q2:B` | Exposed credentials, unauthenticated or public endpoints and excessive privileges are evidence about the system's security and resilience. |
| `third-party-components` | tag `mcp-unpinned-package` or `unsafe-serialization` | `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:GOVERN-6.1`, `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:MANAGE-3.1`, `nist-ai-rmf-1.0:MAP-4.1`, `iso-iec-42001-2023:A.10.3` | Unpinned MCP packages and unsafe model artifacts are third-party components whose risks the organization has to manage. |
